Surah 107: Al-Ma'un

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Have you seen the one who denies the Religion?﴾ That is: Do you know the one who denies the recompense? Who is he, if you do not know him?

Qur'an 107:2 in the commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil):

﴿That is the one who repulses the orphan﴾. He is the one who denies the Recompense. ﴿Repulses the orphan﴾, i.e., he pushes him away with a violent shove, with harshness and harm, and turns him back with a vile rebuff, with rough scolding and roughness.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 107, verse 3:

﴿And does not urge the feeding of the poor.﴾ That is, he does not urge his family to give away food to the poor. He made the sign of denying the Recompense (al-jaza', the Requital) the withholding of kindness (al-ma'ruf) and the readiness to harm the weak. That is: if he had believed in the Recompense and been certain of the threat, he would have feared God and His punishment, and would not have proceeded to such things. So when he did proceed to them, this shows that he is one who denies the Recompense. Then he connected to it His saying:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 107, verses 4–7:

﴿So woe to those who pray﴾ ﴿who are heedless of their prayer﴾ ﴿who make show [of their deeds]﴾ ﴿and withhold [common] kindness﴾. He means by this the hypocrites: that is, they do not pray it in private, because they do not believe in its obligation, and they pray it openly for show. It was also said: "So woe to the hypocrites who include themselves in the ranks of those who pray in appearance, while they are heedless of their prayer, and do not intend by it nearness to their Lord, nor the discharge of an obligation. So they bow and rise, and do not know what they are doing (p-685), and they show people that they perform the obligatory acts, and they withhold zakat and whatever is beneficial."

It is related from Anas and al-Hasan that they both said: "Praise be to Allah who said ﴿heedless of their prayer﴾ and did not say ﴿heedless in their prayer﴾, because the meaning of 'an' (ʿan, 'of/from') is that they are heedless of it, neglecting it and paying it little attention, and that is the act of the hypocrites. The meaning of 'fi' (fi, 'in') is that forgetfulness overtakes them during it, through the whispering of Satan or the talk of the soul, and no believer is free of that." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would himself experience forgetfulness in his prayer, let alone others.

"Al-murā'āh" (ostentation) is a form of "mufā'alah" (reciprocal action) derived from "al-irā'ah" (showing), because the one who makes show of his deed shows it to people, and they show him praise for it and admiration of it. A man is not a show-off merely by making the obligatory acts visible, since it is proper to announce them, due to the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "There is no concealment regarding the obligations of Allah." Concealment is better for voluntary acts; but if he displays them intending to set an example for others to follow, that is commendable.

"Al-māʿūn" (common kindness): zakat. It is also related from Ibn Masʿud (may Allah be pleased with him): "What is customarily lent and borrowed, such as the axe, the cooking pot, the bucket, the flint, and the like." And from ʿAisha (may Allah be pleased with her): "Water, fire, and salt."
